priorStories.headline: U.S. launches AI portal for federal services
priorStories.body:
The federal government launched America.gov, an AI-based interface for finding information and services across government websites.

Its chatbot searches official sources and provides citations with its responses. The site is free, carries no advertising and does not require an account. The government has not identified the AI model behind it.

priorStories.headline: Iran’s currency falls to a record low
priorStories.body:
Traders in Tehran exchanged more than 2.5 million Iranian rials for one U.S. dollar, marking a record low for the currency. The previously reported low was 2.2 million rials per dollar on September 2.

The decline comes as Iran contends with war, international sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade affecting its oil trade.

priorStories.headline: Court permits expedited third-country deportations
priorStories.body:
The Supreme Court temporarily lifted lower-court requirements that people facing deportation to countries other than their own be given an opportunity to object before removal.

The apparent 6-3 order lets the administration continue expedited third-country deportations while the justices review the policy. It does not decide whether the policy is lawful; arguments are scheduled for December.

sources.name: Supreme Court of the United States

candidates.summary: Iranian officials said Tehran received an official U.S. response to its latest proposal for ending the seven-month war. Government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the response to President Masoud Pezeshkian at a Cabinet meeting. Officials did not disclose its contents or say whether it rejected the proposal.
candidates.title: Iran says it received U.S. response to war-ending proposal

candidates.summary: Officials at Shifa and Nasser hospitals said Israeli strikes killed five Palestinians and wounded 19 in Gaza. A strike in Gaza City killed a woman and critically wounded her husband, another struck a bus and killed four people, and a strike in Khan Younis wounded four people.
candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill five Palestinians in Gaza, hospital officials say

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that U.S. consumer prices, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures price index, were 3.4% higher in August than a year earlier. The reading was below economists’ expectations of 3.7%.
candidates.title: U.S. preferred inflation measure rises 3.4% from a year earlier

candidates.summary: The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control designated 10 targets it said were involved in a Tren de Aragua ATM-malware and money-laundering network, along with a separate senior group leader. Treasury said the network stole millions of dollars from U.S. financial institutions and generated revenue for the organization.
candidates.title: U.S. sanctions alleged Tren de Aragua financial network
candidates.geography: United States; Mexico; Venezuela; South America

candidates.summary: The Treasury and Education departments launched an online Defaulted Loans Support Center for people with defaulted federal student loans. The agencies said the portal consolidates information about resolving defaults and returning loans to repayment.
candidates.title: U.S. launches portal for defaulted federal student loans

candidates.summary: Tennessee officials were unable to execute Christa Gail Pike after administering two doses of a lethal-injection drug. She was taken to a medical facility, and Gov. Bill Lee halted the state’s remaining executions for the rest of 2026.
candidates.title: Tennessee execution attempt fails; governor halts remaining 2026 executions

candidates.summary: A copilot stabbed the pilot of a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv and apparently tried to crash the aircraft, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said. Passengers and crew subdued the attacker, and the plane carrying about 170 people landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
candidates.title: Passengers intervene after pilot is stabbed on Israel-bound flight
candidates.geography: Saudi Arabia; United Arab Emirates; Israel

candidates.summary: The U.S. military said it completed the withdrawal of all American troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission against the Islamic State group. The withdrawal was carried out under an agreement reached two years earlier with Iraq.
candidates.title: U.S. military completes troop withdrawal from Iraq

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials said a Russian missile-and-drone barrage killed seven people, including a child, and primarily targeted the country’s power grid. The overnight attack caused power outages as Ukraine prepared for colder weather.
candidates.title: Russian barrage kills seven and targets Ukraine’s power grid

candidates.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a new U.S. military drone command and directed the services to reduce positions for generals and admirals by 20%. Pentagon officials said the senior-rank reduction is to be completed by January 1, 2027.
candidates.title: Pentagon announces drone command and deeper senior-rank cuts

candidates.summary: The State Department removed Syria from a list of countries subject to a general policy of denying licenses and approvals for U.S. weapons and munitions exports. The regulatory change does not itself approve arms sales, which remain subject to licensing.
candidates.title: U.S. removes Syria from general arms-export denial policy

candidates.summary: Republican and Democratic senators announced an agreement on legislation intended to shorten federal reviews for energy and infrastructure projects. The proposal would also require regulators to address the costs that large electricity users, including AI data centers, impose on power systems. A vote was not expected until after the November midterm elections.
candidates.title: U.S. senators reach bipartisan permitting agreement

candidates.summary: Iranian state media said authorities executed two men convicted over violence during nationwide anti-government protests in January. Their death sentences had been upheld by Iran’s Supreme Court, according to the report.
candidates.title: Iran executes two men over alleged roles in January protest violence
